title: Activation Probe Stability Under Distribution Shift of Benign Inputs

original_idea.body:
# Activation Probe Stability Under Distribution Shift of Benign Inputs

Train a logistic-regression jailbreak probe on one open model, then stress-test its false-positive rate across benign domains (clinical, legal, fiction, code) to find which trigger spurious detections. No training of the model; reusable benign stress-test suite (arXiv:2411.09003).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — bridging lab probes to deployment robustness (stated open problem); over-refusal is a concrete silent harm.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: train a logistic-regression probe on activations + stress-test on benign corpora; activation extraction needs ML fundamentals, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped (FPR across benign domains) producing a reusable suite with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open model + public corpora, no internal access, third-party robustness auditing labs underweight.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction on one open model + simple probe, single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe false-positive behavior under benign distribution shift appears explicitly unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Probe FPR under benign distribution shift noted as unstudied.
